scope: Actual public Ara C# Span/Vector128 gameplay versus Unity Editor ECS/Burst: W1 and W3, Mac, optimized Release modules only
quality: All 1,000,000 stable IDs/native handles and required components checked; every component field compared bitwise to independent scalar replay. Complete 48,000,000-byte final dumps equal Unity byte for byte in every pair. No math/precision approximation.

method.ara_runtime: CoreCLR 10.0.14, image observed before setup_complete in all eight runs
method.ara_module: cold optimized Release, explicit Vector128 math, tiered compilation disabled
method.unity: 6000.4.5f1, Burst1.8.29, Entities/Collections6.4.0; effective worker options checked and restored
method.resources: sequential fresh processes, nice10, AC power stable at every 1s sample (Unity2s); unrelated compiler/Unity checks; owned compile-server descendants recorded separately

limits: Only these two dense arithmetic workloads; not total frame/startup, boids, structural, buffer or dependency coverage.
Hot Debug after edit was checked for correctness but not timed here.
Two process samples per case; means of process percentiles are descriptive, not confidence intervals.
Explicit SIMD math differs from the original slower native fixture implementation; this is a usable public C# API example, not a production engine-wide speedup.
OS scheduling and unrelated work below sampled guards remain uncontrolled.
Shipping NativeAOT and Windows performance not measured in this packet.
